chapters.title: Thermoregulation and Osmoregulation
chapters.main_concept: Introduces homeostasis as the maintenance of a stable internal environment through receptors, control centres and effectors operating by negative and positive feedback, then applies it to water/solute balance (osmoregulation, nitrogenous excretion by habitat) and body-temperature regulation in animals and humans.

subtopics.title: Nature of Excretory Products in relation to Habitat
Types of Animals on the basis of Heat Source
Types of Animals on the basis of Thermoregulation

formulas: Homeostatic loop: stimulus -> receptor -> control centre -> effector -> response (restores set point)
Ammonia NH3; uric acid C5H4N4O3
Water needed to excrete 1 g waste: ammonia ~500 mL, urea ~50 mL, uric acid ~1 mL
Normal human core temperature 37 °C (98.6 °F)

chapters.title: Human Urinary System
chapters.main_concept: Describes the organs of the human urinary system, kidney and nephron structure, renal blood supply, and urine formation (filtration, reabsorption, secretion), regulation of urine concentration by the counter-current mechanism and hormones (ADH, aldosterone), and common disorders with treatments (UTI, stones, kidney failure, dialysis, transplant).
formulas: Urine formation = glomerular filtration -> selective reabsorption -> tubular secretion
~20% of plasma filters into Bowman's capsule; ~75% water reabsorbed in PCT
Kidneys receive ~20-25% of cardiac output; ~1 million nephrons per kidney; cortical nephrons ~85%
Adult urine output 1-2 L/day
Stone type vs urine pH: alkaline -> calcium phosphate; acidic -> uric acid/cystine; calcium oxalate pH-independent

chapters.title: Human Nervous System
chapters.main_concept: Explains nervous coordination: receptors, neurons (structure, types, reflex arc), generation and propagation of nerve impulses, synaptic transmission and neurotransmitters, organization of CNS and PNS, sensory receptors (taste, smell, touch, pain), effects of psychoactive drugs (addiction, tolerance, withdrawal), nervous disorders by category, and diagnostic tests (EEG, CT, MRI).

chapters.title: Human Reproductive System
chapters.main_concept: Describes male and female reproductive organs and their functions, spermatogenesis and oogenesis, hormonal control of male reproduction (GnRH, FSH, LH, testosterone, inhibin) and the phases and hormonal regulation of the menstrual cycle.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.main_concept: Extends Mendelian genetics: laws of segregation and independent assortment with probability rules, deviations (incomplete dominance, co-dominance, multiple alleles, polygenic inheritance, epistasis), human blood group systems (ABO, Rh, MN) and erythroblastosis foetalis, gene linkage and crossing over, sex determination systems, sex-linked, sex-limited and sex-influenced traits, X-linked disorders and embryonic screening.

chapters.title: Chromosome and DNA
chapters.main_concept: Covers detailed chromosome morphology and packaging, experimental proof of DNA as hereditary material (Griffith, Avery et al., Hershey-Chase), DNA replication models and the Meselson-Stahl experiment, the replication mechanism, gene expression (genetic code, transcription with post-transcriptional modification, translation), regulation of gene expression, and mutations (point and chromosomal) with associated human disorders.

Methods of Regulation: transcriptional level (negative/positive), during splicing

formulas: Chromosome ~40% DNA, ~60% protein; ~146 bp per nucleosome; linker ~80 bp
Packing: DNA 2 nm -> nucleosome string 11 nm -> chromatin fibre 30 nm -> supercoil 300 nm -> chromatid 700 nm (1400 nm chromosome)

Codons: 4^3 = 64 (61 sense, 3 stop: UAA, UAG, UGA); start AUG = Met
Okazaki fragments: prokaryotes 1000-2000 nt, eukaryotes 100-200 nt
Down 47 (2n+1, trisomy 21); Klinefelter 47 (44+XXY); Turner 45 (44+XO)

chapters.title: Immunity
chapters.main_concept: Describes the body's three lines of defence: physical/chemical barriers (skin, digestive and respiratory tracts), non-specific internal defences (phagocytes, NK cells, complement, interferons, inflammation, fever), and the specific immune system (monocytes, T and B cells; cell-mediated and antibody-mediated immunity, antibody structure, monoclonal antibodies), plus types of immunity and immune disorders (allergies, autoimmunity, transplant rejection).

chapters.title: Biostatistics
chapters.main_concept: Defines biostatistics, its components and applications in health and biology, then teaches calculation of mean, median, mode, standard deviation, range and percentile with worked examples, construction of bar charts, pie charts, x-axis data figures and error bars, and the principles of experimental design (variables, control and experimental groups).

subtopics.title: Study Design and Experimental Planning; Data Collection; Data Management; Data Analysis; Interpretation; Presentation

topics.title: Key Statistical Measures and their Calculation

subtopics.title: Error Bars (range and SD error bars)
Experiment: Effect of high-fat diet on weight gain in albino mice

formulas: Mean (ungrouped) = Σx / n; Mean (grouped) = Σ(f·x) / Σf (x = class midpoint)
Median: odd n -> value at (n+1)/2; even n -> average of values at n/2 and n/2+1
Mode (grouped) = l + [(fm - f1) / ((fm - f1) + (fm - f2))] × h
Standard deviation σ = sqrt[ Σ(x - μ)^2 / N ]; variance = σ^2
Range = Xmax - Xmin
Percentile rank R = (P/100) × (n + 1); interpolate if non-integer
Pie sector angle = (category value / total) × 360°

chapters.title: Evolution
chapters.main_concept: Presents evolution as change in allele frequencies driven by variation and natural selection: Darwin's observations and theory, Neo-Darwinism and the Hardy-Weinberg theorem with factors changing allele frequencies, evidences from biogeography, comparative anatomy and molecular biology, the endosymbiotic origin of eukaryotes, and Lamarckism with its drawbacks.

chapters.title: Ecology
chapters.main_concept: Covers levels of ecological organization, biogeochemical cycles and their reservoirs (water and nitrogen cycles in detail), energy flow and loss across trophic levels, population characteristics (survivorship, growth models, density, dispersion, carrying capacity, minimum viable size), human population growth and its impacts, the greenhouse effect and its harmful effects (with Pakistan examples), and four important ecosystems of Pakistan.
